thread:
maya: quick heads-up — after the autoscaler changes this morning we saw a bunch of traces missing parent spans for requests routed to GPU pools :thinking_face:

sam: saw that too. metric spike in request.latency.gpu around 10:12 UTC and traces just break at the gateway hop

liam: do we know if headers are being dropped by the autoscaler nginx proxy? that usually strips grpc metadata unless we pass them explicitly

maya: I grabbed a tcpdump earlier, looks like the otel-traceparent header is present on inbound, gone on the upstream call to runtime. log snippet:

maya: ```
[10:12:04.123] gateway: recv traceparent=00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01
[10:12:04.125] gateway: upstream call headers: (traceparent missing)
```

nina: tracked this to a config change in the autoscaler helm chart — we switched to the new http-proxy image and removed `preserve_host` and `proxy_set_header` overrides when moving to xDS

liam: ugh. that would explain it. if the proxy rewrites the headers they won't reach the runtime and the SDK can't link spans

sam: aside — this makes debugging slow GPU batches annoying: Prom dashboard shows GPU_util high, end-to-end latency up, but traces don't tie together so we can't tell if it's queueing at gateway vs runtime

maya: opened a quick PR to add `proxy_set_header traceparent $http_traceparent;` and same for `tracestate` and `baggage` to the autoscaler chart: https://git.internal/redwood/autoscaler/pull/492 :pr

deploy-bot: deploy queued — autoscaler-proxy 2.3.7 -> 2.3.8 — canary to dev first :rocket:

sam: meanwhile can we add a unit test to the runtime infra tests that asserts trace headers survive a proxy hop? simple curl to gateway -> check runtime logs for trace id

liam: yeah i'll add an integration test in eng-runtime CI. snippet i'll use:

liam: ```bash
curl -H "traceparent: 00-11112222333344445555666677778888-0123456789abcdef-01" http://gateway.dev.internal/healthz
grep "11112222" runtime.log || exit 1
```

nina: also adding a Grafana alert tweak — alert: TraceLinkFailureRate — if >0.5% of requests have missing parent span over 5m then critical. will route to pager for CUSTOMER_SLO_P1

maya: nice. but let's be careful with noise — a small rollout could trigger false positives. can we make it warning at 0.5% and critical at 2%?

nina: good call. set warning=0.5% critical=2% and add runbook link to dashboard

sam: related cost note — when tracing disappears we can't attribute high GPU spend to specific routes. finance flagged a 12% bump in gpu-hours for prod cluster last month and asked for tracing-backed breakdowns

maya: i'll pull a correlation report between gpu-hours and trace-link failures for the last 30 days and share in #finance. if autoprofiler can't link spans, we should fall back to request-level metrics with route tags

liam: added a small fallback in runtime: if parent missing, attach `trace.link_status=missing` tag to the span and emit metric `tracing.link_missing_total{route=\"<route>\"}` so we can at least count

sam: awesome. once the canary finishes let's watch the tracelink metric and the GPU SLO dashboard: https://grafana.internal/d/abcd123/gpu-slo?orgId=1

maya: canary passed on dev. rolling to prod in 10m. thanks all :thumbsup:

ops-bot: prod rollout started for autoscaler-proxy 2.3.8 by maya — monitoring: TraceLinkFailureRate, request.latency.gpu, gpu_utilization

maya: prod rollout done. initial checks look green but watching for 30m

nina: saw TraceLinkFailureRate drop to 0.03% and traces start linking again. will follow up with a postmortem doc and add the new tests to the CI matrix

sam: can we add a checklist item to onboarding for infra changes that affect headers/metadata? small config change nearly broke a whole observability chain

maya: agreed. adding `observability-impact` checkbox to infra change template and PR template now

liam: documenting the test and the Grafana thresholds in runbook: https://wiki.internal/redwood/observability/runbooks/trace-propagation

maya: closing this thread — if anyone sees anomalies ping here and i'll reopen

nina: thanks, team :)
